title: New screenshot tool — do its Settings pictures match the old one's?

steps.headline: Appearance looks the same from both tools, pixel for pixel.
steps.changed: The new tool opens Appearance by its name instead of clicking the gear and then the row. 32 of the 34 pictures both tools took were identical like this one.
steps.notice: Nothing — the picture you review is the same. It just arrives faster, and cannot break when a button is renamed.

steps.headline: A screen two levels deep also matches exactly.
steps.changed: The new tool opens the bug report form straight away. The old one clicked Settings, then Development, then the report row.
steps.notice: Same picture, fewer steps that could go wrong.

steps.headline: Backup & Sync matches too, and the new tool waits for it to finish loading.
steps.changed: This panel shows a spinner first. The new tool waits until the real panel is on screen instead of guessing a time.
steps.notice: No more pictures of a half-loaded panel.

steps.headline: The Settings drawer matches; only the theme's moving background dots differ.
steps.changed: The drawer itself is the same. These two themes animate their background, so the dots were caught at a different moment.
steps.notice: Pictures of animated themes will always differ a little in the background, from either tool.
steps.risk: A real change hidden in a moving background is easy to miss; the new tool's automatic check does not compare pictures, only that each screen opened.

steps.headline: The old tool could no longer open Cloud providers. The new one can.
steps.changed: The old tool's plan clicked a button name that changed, so it failed. The new tool opens the page by its name.
steps.notice: A renamed button no longer breaks the pictures.

steps.headline: Performance had never been photographed. Now it is.
steps.changed: This row only appears on computers with two graphics chips. The practice copy can now pretend to be one of those.
steps.notice: One more Settings screen you can review.
steps.risk: The two chip names shown are made up for the practice copy.

steps.headline: Help & feedback had no plan in the old tool. Every Settings screen is now covered.
steps.changed: All 21 Settings screens are in the new tool's list, including this one, which the old tool never had.
steps.measured: 21 screens, 42 pictures in 19 seconds; the old tool took 58 seconds for 36
steps.notice: Asking for 'every Settings screen' now really means every one.
